claim: Gross mean concentric force per unit mass is the time average of vertical ground-reaction force per kilogram from concentric onset to takeoff: F_bar = (1/T) integral Fz/m dt.
forbidden_wording: peak force; net force; 'peak mean force'

claim: Concentric net impulse per unit mass is the integral of (Fz/m - g) over the concentric phase; with mean force it equals (F_bar - g)*T.
forbidden_wording: gross impulse; momentum in N s

claim: Standard gravity used by the synthetic system is 9.80665 m/s^2.

In the synthetic system each trial is a 65-node half-sine net-force pulse of duration T = J/(F_bar - g), with T constrained to 0.075-0.80 s; peak force equals g + (pi/2)(F_bar - g) for the continuous half-sine.
forbidden_wording: observed athlete force-time curve; empirical waveform shape

claim: An assessment is the arithmetic mean of exactly three valid trials; the baseline is a dedicated three-trial assessment about two hours before exposure.
The modeled target is baseline-relative innovation: criterion-assessment mean minus baseline-assessment mean, additive, in N/kg for force and m/s for impulse; never pooled across units.
The registered key relative_peak_mean_force_innovation is a legacy identifier for mean concentric-force innovation, not peak force.
permitted_wording: legacy identifier for mean concentric-force innovation

claim: Mode amplitudes are bounded: a_f in [0.01, 0.08], a_s in [0, 0.08], from a sigmoid of exposure axes, participant sensitivity and camp offsets.

A bounded smooth shared discrepancy (amplitude fraction 0.006, 32 random Fourier features) and per-episode discrepancy (0.0030-0.0080) perturb the nominal modes.
Training stream: 96 camps, 24,000 episodes, 72,000 horizon rows; development: 16 camps, 4,000 episodes, 12,000 rows.
